beats.spoken: What happens when a cream causes a serious undesirable effect?
EU law defines what serious means: an effect that leads to temporary or permanent functional incapacity, disability, hospitalisation, congenital anomalies, an immediate risk to life, or death.

For these cases, Article 23 applies. The responsible person and distributors notify the competent authority without delay: the effect, the exact product name and any corrective action. The authority then informs the other member states.

nodes.text: passed on to other member states

beats.spoken: Consumers and health professionals can contact the authority too. The authority then passes the information on to the other member states and to the responsible person.

In the US, MoCRA brought a similar duty. The responsible person reports serious adverse events to the FDA within 15 business days. New information within a year also has to follow within 15 business days.
For you, that means: with a serious reaction, get medical help first. For a report, the exact product name and the batch number from the pack will help.
Read the pack first, then apply. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
